about: Every external data source and service MapUnite uses: its licence, attribution, whether commercial use is allowed, how it's accessed, and the legal review status. test/server/data-sources.test.mjs fails if code calls a host that isn't listed here. Nothing below is legal advice: every entry is 'pending' until someone qualified has checked the current terms. 'unclear' means we haven't confirmed it: treat as not cleared for commercial use.

sources.name: OpenStreetMap data (via Nominatim, Overpass, OSRM, road extracts)
sources.use: place search, POIs and speed limits (Overpass), named places drawn on the map (/api/map/places, lib/map-detail.js), the road index for hazard merging (data/roads)
sources.access_method: public APIs at request time; offline extract for data/roads
sources.notes: Data is commercially usable with attribution; share-alike applies to derivative databases. Review before selling an API or publishing a database built on it (derivative vs collective database). The public Nominatim and Overpass servers have usage policies (Nominatim: max 1 request/s, no bulk): self-host for production.

sources.name: OpenStreetMap standard tiles
sources.use: the street base layer
sources.licence: ODbL (data) / CC BY-SA 2.0 (cartography, check current terms)
sources.notes: The OSMF tile usage policy does not allow heavy production use of tile.openstreetmap.org: move to self-hosted or a commercial tile provider before launch.

sources.name: OSRM demo server
sources.use: routing
sources.licence: OSRM software BSD-2-Clause; routes from OSM data (ODbL)
sources.notes: A demo server, not meant for production traffic: self-host OSRM (or another engine) with an OSM extract before launch.

sources.name: OpenTopoMap tiles
sources.use: the terrain base layer
sources.licence: CC BY-SA 3.0 (map style); data OSM (ODbL) and SRTM
sources.attribution: Map data: © OpenStreetMap contributors, SRTM | Map style: © OpenTopoMap (CC-BY-SA)
sources.notes: A volunteer-run server: check its fair-use terms; self-host for production.

sources.name: Esri World Imagery
sources.use: the satellite base layer (default), its road and place-name label layers (Reference/World_Transportation, Reference/World_Boundaries_and_Places), and the post-ride review map
sources.notes: Check Esri's current terms for use in a commercial app (account or licence may be needed). The label layers' exact credit line (Esri's data providers) must be copied from each service's copyright text before launch.

sources.name: CARTO dark basemap
sources.use: the dark base layer, Ride Focus AMOLED, and the map behind the route on ride recap cards (Dark Matter and Voyager, drawn on the phone into the image the rider shares)
sources.notes: Check CARTO's current limits for free vs commercial use, and whether map images in user-shared recap cards need anything beyond the attribution drawn on them ("© OpenStreetMap contributors © CARTO").

sources.name: Open-Meteo weather and air quality APIs
sources.use: weather on the route, the advice gate's wet-road check, air quality
sources.licence: data CC BY 4.0; API terms: the free API is for non-commercial use
sources.notes: Commercial use needs an Open-Meteo subscription, or self-hosting the open-source Open-Meteo with openly licensed model data (NOAA GFS, ECMWF open data). IMD data needs its own agreement.

sources.name: MET Norway Locationforecast 2.0
sources.use: the Ride Plan's ride-day forecast (lib/master/metno.js), fetched by our server only and cached per ~1 km cell for 30 minutes
sources.licence: data CC BY 4.0 and NLOD 2.0; api.met.no terms of service
sources.access_method: HTTP API from the server (User-Agent with app name and contact, coordinates ≤ 4 decimals)
sources.notes: Free, commercial use allowed with attribution. Terms: identify the app in User-Agent (MET_NO_USER_AGENT), cache, no more than 20 requests/second per app. Hourly steps for ~2.5 days, then 6-hourly to ~9-10 days.

sources.name: NASA POWER climatology (Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources)
sources.use: the Ride Plan's usual weather for a month (lib/master/nasapower.js) when no forecast reaches the ride day; never shown as a forecast
sources.licence: NASA open data (no restrictions; credit requested)
sources.access_method: HTTP API from the server, no key; cached per 0.5° cell for 30 days
sources.notes: Long-term monthly means on a ~55 km grid: a regional pattern, not the road. Confirm the credit wording on power.larc.nasa.gov before launch.

sources.name: Government hospital directory with geo-codes (e.g. National Hospital Directory on data.gov.in)
sources.use: known hospital locations along a route in the Ride Plan (lib/master/hospitals.js), imported by scripts/master/import-hospitals.mjs
sources.licence: Government Open Data License - India (check the dataset page)
sources.attribution: the dataset's publisher, as named on data.gov.in
sources.access_method: manual download, imported on the server
sources.notes: Shown as KNOWN locations, never verified: directories go stale and geo-codes are approximate. Nothing is imported yet (data/master/hospitals/README.md).

sources.name: MapUnite riders' place ratings
sources.use: riders' 👍/👎 and tags for OSM places they said they stopped at (lib/master/place-ratings.js), shown in the Ride Plan from 3 ratings
sources.notes: Opt-in after a ride, never automatic from a stop; pseudonymous rater (HMAC of a phone token); fixed tags, no free text; deletable with /api/master/ratings/forget.

sources.name: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (ESA / European Union)
sources.use: the self-hosted 30 m terrain model for the pilot corridors (lib/elevation/, scripts/elevation-ingest.mjs): route gradients, the gradient sheet, trip energy, valley-edge warnings
sources.licence: Copernicus DEM licence (GLO-30 public release): free of charge, worldwide, including commercial use and redistribution of derived products, with the credit below
sources.attribution: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 © DLR e.V. 2010-2014 and © Airbus Defence and Space GmbH 2014-2018, provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA
sources.access_method: downloaded once per corridor by scripts/elevation-ingest.mjs from the AWS Open Data bucket (public, no account); served from our own server; never fetched by the phone
sources.notes: Each corridor's <id>.json records the files used and their SHA-256. The credit is sent with every elevation answer and shown in the gradient sheet. Copy the exact credit wording from the licence PDF on the Copernicus Data Space before launch (the line here follows the AWS registry's). Heights are a surface model (trees and roofs included), relative to the EGM2008 geoid.

sources.name: NASADEM (NASA JPL, 1 arc-second)
sources.use: the alternative source for the 30 m terrain model (scripts/elevation-ingest.mjs --source nasadem --from <dir>)
sources.licence: NASA data: no restrictions on use (NASA Earthdata data use policy); downloading needs a free Earthdata login
sources.attribution: NASADEM courtesy of NASA JPL and the NASA EOSDIS Land Processes DAAC
sources.access_method: downloaded by hand with an Earthdata login (the script never fetches it), served from our own server
sources.notes: Not used unless chosen: Copernicus is the default. NASA asks for a citation of the dataset in publications; the credit line is shown in the app like Copernicus's.

sources.name: Google Maps Platform (Places, Maps)
sources.use: the Maps script tag, place lookups (server-side keys), ratings and reviews for the Master AI's vetted places (off with MASTER_POI_GOOGLE=0), and the optional Google map style; the Ride Plan uses none of it (Map Tiles API, proxied by lib/map-detail.js, off unless GOOGLE_MAP_TILES_KEY is set)
sources.licence: Google Maps Platform Terms of Service
sources.access_method: paid API with a server-side key
sources.notes: Paid, under Google's terms (no caching or scraping beyond them). RoadPulse data must never be mixed with Google content. Map Tiles: the server passes tiles through with Google's cache headers and stores none; Google's logo and the viewport copyright line must show while the Google style is on (the app shows a text logo: replace with Google's official logo asset before launch). Check whether a server-side tile proxy is allowed under the current Map Tiles terms.

sources.name: Google Cloud Text-to-Speech
sources.use: premium voice (optional, server-side)
sources.access_method: paid API with a server-side key
sources.notes: Optional: the phone's own TTS works without it.

sources.name: ElevenLabs TTS
sources.use: premium voice (optional, server-side)
sources.access_method: paid API with a server-side key
sources.notes: Optional.

sources.name: Google Gemini API
sources.use: Deep Search answers (optional; never road facts: 'sensors verify, language models talk')
sources.notes: The product direction is to depend on no third-party AI keys: keep optional, plan to remove or self-host.

sources.name: Groq API
sources.use: language-model answers (optional)
sources.notes: Same as Gemini: optional, planned for removal or self-hosting.

sources.name: TomTom Traffic API
sources.use: traffic flow (optional, server-side)
sources.access_method: paid API with a server-side key
sources.notes: Optional.

sources.name: BigDataCloud reverse geocoding
sources.use: city name from a position
sources.notes: Check whether the free client-side endpoint allows commercial apps.

sources.name: Last.fm API
sources.use: music suggestions (optional)
sources.notes: Check the API terms for commercial use.

sources.name: Front-end libraries and fonts from CDNs (Leaflet, fonts)
sources.use: map library (Leaflet BSD-2-Clause), web fonts (SIL OFL)
sources.licence: per library: Leaflet BSD-2-Clause; fonts SIL OFL 1.1
sources.access_method: CDN at load time (the service worker caches them)
sources.notes: Licences allow commercial use; consider self-hosting for offline-first and privacy (no third-party requests).

sources.name: RoadPulse rider reports and reviews
sources.use: the public hazard layer
sources.notes: Contributor terms must grant MapUnite the right to store, show and license the reports (needed before any API sale), and say what is public (spot, direction, kind, severity, day) and what never is (route, identity).
